_comment: Targets measured to be degenerate — tlapm discharges the PROOF OBVIOUS
placeholder untouched, so a no-op submission would PASS grading — but that
the triviality gate does not detect reliably.
The gate runs 16 tlapm at once, each able to start a multi-GB Isabelle, and
its verdict under that load is not reproducible: over the same 451-task
suite one pass timed out on 128 tasks and another on none, and the SAME
quiet machine) or '1/1 obligation failed ... There were backend errors'.
A timeout is re-checked on the grader's budget, which catches the first
shape; a crashed backend is indistinguishable in tlapm's output from an
honest refutation (the banner appears on 415 of 486 tasks), so it cannot be
Listing a target here makes the drop deterministic instead of leaving it to
the machine's mood. Each entry records how it was measured, so it can be
rechecked after a tlapm or backend upgrade. Same policy as
duplicate_task_families.json: a judgement a human made, recorded in the
repository rather than re-derived per run.
